directive:
**Discovery** — establish the project's context one topic at a time, each a markdown file at `discovery/<topic>.md` (canonical key = the file stem). The REQUIRED set is DYNAMIC: the baseline `goal, scope, stack, architecture, users, release` is seeded for you — shape it for THIS project with `bsc plan discovery require <topic>` / `bsc plan discovery unrequire <topic>` as the picture clarifies (a CLI tool unrequires `users`/`ux`; a data platform requires `schema`; a realtime API requires `api`). `bsc plan discovery list` shows the manifest. The `release` file proposes the versioning + release schedule: default to a COMPLETE initial prototype first, then FEATURE-BY-FEATURE releases (semver; release-and-continue). ALWAYS write the required files; cover other dimensions ONLY where they genuinely apply, using the canonical key as the file stem (`discovery/ux.md`, `discovery/schema.md`, `discovery/api.md`, `discovery/security.md`, `discovery/testing.md`, `discovery/observability.md`, `discovery/reliability.md`, `discovery/data_lifecycle.md`, …; the production-readiness bars in the planning guide are first-class dimensions here — apply where they matter, accessibility/compliance via the Compliance MCP, and **SEO for any public web-facing project** (`discovery/seo.md` — target audience/keywords + indexability; the **Web SEO** skill carries the how; skip it for CLI/desktop/library/internal/API-only)). When the project hinges on specialized or fast-moving techniques (graphics, algorithms, ML, cryptography, distributed systems, physics), ground the `stack`/`architecture` choices using the Research workflow in the planning guide rather than guessing. Record every dimension you don't document in `discovery/_skipped.md`. The required files are done once WRITTEN — they're generated, not confirmed (the gate checks every required `discovery/<topic>.md` exists). Do NOT create files for tangential topics, or the gate can't complete.

**Classify the project (the closing step of Discovery).** Once the picture is clear, record the classification with `bsc plan classify set` (a JSON object on stdin) — this shapes the rest of the plan: (1) `lifecycle` — what this planning run is FOR: `greenfield` (build from a pitch), `transform` (restructure existing repos), `harden` (improve an existing codebase in place), `maintain` (keep a shipped system running). INFER it from what you already know rather than asking — linked repos you are restructuring means `transform`, a bare pitch means `greenfield`; (2) `appType` — the app's ARCHITECTURE, the axis that selects WHICH STAGES RUN: `application` (a general app with screens), `desktop`, `mobile`, `static` (a site), `api` (a backend service), `serverless` (functions), `cli` (a command-line tool), `library` (a published package), `mcp-server` (an MCP server). The UI stage DROPS for the types with no screens (`api`, `serverless`, `cli`, `library`, `mcp-server`), so get this right or the plan designs screens nothing will ever render; (3) `uiMode` — `custom` if the UI is generated IN-APP (the designer builds a live, navigable shell you preview as you plan — the default for most apps) or `external` if the user brings their own design files to drop in; (4) which of the OFF-by-default OPTIONAL stages the project genuinely needs — `needsMarket` (a desk-research market assessment is worth doing), `needsSource` (migrating data FROM a legacy system: a CRM/ERP/SaaS/database), `needsMcp` (the fleet's agents need external tools or data via MCP servers), `needsSkills` (a reusable skill library is worth authoring for this project), `needsAutomations` (scheduled / cron jobs). MOST projects need NONE of the optional stages — turn one on ONLY if the project truly requires it, and ASK the user to confirm before enabling (enabling a stage makes it appear in the plan for you to complete). Examples: `{"lifecycle":"greenfield","appType":"application","uiMode":"custom"}` for a simple app; `{"lifecycle":"greenfield","appType":"mcp-server"}` for an MCP server (no UI stage); `{"lifecycle":"transform","appType":"api","needsSource":true}` for a data migration. Then DECLARE this app's contracts with OTHER PROJECTS — with `bsc project link add <this-project-key> <other-project-key> <api|data|events>` — so the relationship shows in Glance and downstream agents know the contract. Record ONLY real dependencies. Example: `bsc project link add storefront billing-api api`. **PROJECT-TO-PROJECT ONLY.** The Glance network models the ESTATE — the projects and how they relate. Do NOT declare the external services, APIs, or SDKs an app talks to (Stripe, GitHub, an LLM provider, a push service, a relay): those are implementation details INSIDE one application, not members of the estate, and drawing them as nodes says the estate is composed of them. They belong in `discovery/architecture.md` as prose. If the other side is not itself a project in this workspace, it is not a link.

blurb: Discovery — the fundamental files that give Claude a clear picture (goal, scope, stack, architecture, users, versioning & release schedule + applicable dimensions).
prompt:
Establish the project's context — one topic at a time — as a markdown file per topic at
`discovery/<topic>.md` (the canonical key is the file stem). The REQUIRED set is dynamic and
project-specific: the baseline `goal, scope, stack, architecture, users, release` is seeded for
you, but shape it for THIS project with `bsc plan discovery require <topic>` / `bsc plan discovery
unrequire <topic>` as the picture clarifies — e.g. a CLI tool unrequires `users`/`ux`; a data
platform requires `schema`; a realtime API requires `api`. `bsc plan discovery list` shows the
required set.

For each topic: propose it, interrogate it with the user, then WRITE the file. Cover non-required
dimensions only where they genuinely apply (canonical keys: ux, schema, api, auth, security,
testing, …); record the rest in `discovery/_skipped.md`. Finish each file fully — no TODO / TBD /
FIXME / XXX / TKTK markers (the gate blocks on them; ordinary "..." or "placeholder" is fine).

The discovery files are done once GENERATED — they don't need confirmation; the gate passes when
every required topic's file exists.

As the CLOSING step of Discovery, CLASSIFY the project with `bsc plan classify set` (JSON on stdin):
set `uiMode` (`custom` = an in-app generated UI, the default; `external` = the user brings design
files), and turn ON only the OPTIONAL stages this project genuinely needs — `needsMarket` (a
desk-research market assessment), `needsSource` (migrating from a legacy system), `needsMcp` (agents
need external tools via MCP servers), `needsSkills` (a reusable skill library), `needsAutomations`
(scheduled jobs). Most projects need NONE — ASK the user before turning one on; enabling a stage makes
it appear in the plan. Then DECLARE this app's contracts with OTHER PROJECTS in this workspace, with
`bsc project link add <this-project-key> <other-project-key> <api|data|events>` — record ONLY real
dependencies. PROJECT-TO-PROJECT ONLY: the Glance network models the estate, so do NOT link the
external services or APIs an app merely talks to (Stripe, GitHub, an LLM provider, a push service) —
those live inside one application and belong in `discovery/architecture.md` as prose, not as nodes.

Gate: every required topic is written.

substeps.label: Goal
substeps.prompt:
Establish the goal: the single outcome this project must achieve, and who it's for. Propose
it, interrogate it with the user, then write `discovery/goal.md`.

substeps.label: Scope
substeps.prompt:
Define what's in scope and — just as important — what's explicitly out of scope. Write
`discovery/scope.md`.

substeps.label: Stack
substeps.prompt:
Decide the technology stack — languages, frameworks, datastores — and the reasoning behind
each choice. Write it to the file named exactly `discovery/stack.md` (not "tech stack.md" or a
titled variant — the gate looks for the `stack` stem).

substeps.label: Architecture
substeps.prompt:
Describe the high-level architecture: the major components and how they interact. Write
`discovery/architecture.md`.

substeps.label: Users
substeps.prompt:
Describe who uses this — the user roles/personas and what each needs from the app. Write
`discovery/users.md`. (Unrequire this with `bsc plan discovery unrequire users` if the project genuinely has no distinct users, e.g. a pure CLI or library.)

substeps.label: Versioning & release schedule
substeps.prompt:
Propose an ideal versioning scheme and release schedule for THIS project, then write
`discovery/release.md`. Default to the shape that fits how this app is built: ship a COMPLETE initial
prototype first — one early version (e.g. `0.1.0` / `v1.0.0`) that delivers the whole thing working
end-to-end at a basic level, the foundation everything else builds on — and from there release
FEATURE BY FEATURE, one focused increment per version. Use semver: patch for fixes, minor for each
feature release, major for breaking changes. Recommend a release-and-continue rhythm — ship a
version early and keep refining it until its theme is complete before moving to the next. Lay out
the first few concrete versions: the prototype, then the next 2–4 feature versions in order, each
with a one-line theme. Adapt the cadence to the goal/scope/users (a regulated or data-migration
product may need longer, gated releases) and confirm the shape with the user before writing.

substeps.label: Applicable dimensions
substeps.prompt:
Now cover any remaining dimension that genuinely applies — one at a time — using the canonical
key as the file stem (`discovery/ux.md`, `discovery/schema.md`, `discovery/api.md`, `discovery/auth.md`,
`discovery/security.md`, `discovery/testing.md`, …); `bsc plan discovery require <topic>` any you want
to gate on. Record every dimension you don't document in `discovery/_skipped.md`. Don't create files
for tangential topics.
